module: Optional routing layer placed in front of the camera input path. Registered 'controllers' (by id, with priority) can consume certain inputs (e.g. onRelativeInput, onEditorMouseWheel) when they are active; whatever is not consumed continues to the active camera as before. Loaded with require('core/cameraControllerRegistry') (it is not an extension). Used by core/cameraInput.lua. A modder uses it to intercept the mouse/wheel (e.g. a camera editing tool) without breaking normal cameras.
notes: A controller is a table whose keys are method names (e.g. onRelativeInput, onEditorMouseWheel); a method consumes the event by returning exactly true.
Call order: descending priority, then alphabetical id. If a controller has 'captured' (acquire), only that one receives events.

acquire is only allowed if no other has captured and if the caller is the controller currently being dispatched, or the first in the order (highest priority): so you can only capture from your own callback or by being first.
unregister automatically releases the capture if that controller held it.

register.desc: Registers a controller. Fails (false) if the id is not a non-empty string, if controller is not a table or if the id already exists.

unregister.desc: Removes a controller. If controller is given, it must match the registered one. Releases the capture if needed.

dispatch.desc: Sends an event to the controllers: to the capture owner only if there is one, otherwise to all in order until one returns true.

method.desc: Name of the method to call on the controllers

returns.desc: true if a controller consumed the event

acquire.desc: Takes exclusive capture of the inputs for this controller (see notes for the conditions).

returns.desc: true if the capture is (or already was) held by this controller

release.desc: Releases the capture if this controller holds it.

isOwner.desc: Tests whether this controller holds the capture.

isRegistered.desc: Tests whether the id is registered (and, if controller is given, that it is this controller).
